reasons: A implements the wrong algorithm: it gives the 10-digit INN two control digits and checks the 12-digit INN at positions 10-11 with the 12th digit left unchecked, so real valid INNs such as 7707083893 would be rejected and its 'valid' test vectors are invalid. B uses the correct FNS weights for both lengths, and its test vectors (7707083893, 500100000199) do pass the checksum. Both answers claim test runs they could not perform; B's fabricated log also has duplicated lines, but this matters much less than A's broken core logic.

A: Claims a 10-digit INN has two control digits computed with weights (2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6) and (7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6); the real FNS algorithm has a single control digit using weights 2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8
Claims the 12th digit of a 12-digit INN is an unchecked serial number; it is the second control digit (weights 3,7,2,4,10,3,5,9,4,6,8)
Test vectors 7700000097, 5024000141, 770000000931 and 780502133497 are described as valid but fail the real FNS checksum
